full_judgment: 9. It is in this context that this Court is now laced with impugned judgment of the learned joint District Judge which in reversing the trial Court's judgment came to a finding, inter alia, that though the prima facts title of the petitioners predecessors in interests could be proven before the trial Court there is the outstanding question of actual and uninterrupted possession of the land by the petitioners which thereby proved fatal to the petitioners case at the appellant stage. It is not clear to this Court as to how and why the learned District Judge came to take issue with the question of possession, given the fact that the judgment of the trial Court amply discussed the issue and disposed of the same with an express finding upon a consideration of the evidence on record as corroborated by the PWs. That difficulty, in the view of this Court, stems primarily from the lack of discussion of evidence, oral and documentary, by the lower appellate Court to support its finding in this regard. In other words, that judgment is not ably served by definite and specific findings supported by reasoned consideration of evidence. In the absence of cogent reasoning or of clear findings on any issue of fact and law in the impugned judgment, this Court in revision has been hard pressed to best understand the correctness or general drift and gist of the impugned judgment. This Court finds that in that regard the impugned judgment fails far short of the standard in Order 41, rule XXXI of the Code. Considering the specificity of the findings of the trial Court based on full consideration of facts and evidence, this Court fails to see why the impugned judgment or reversal is so marked by its back of elaboration to any level of satisfaction of the reasons no reversing the trial Court's judgment. Moreover, and on the basis of this Court's reading of relevant facts, and oral and documentary evidence, this Court also finds that the learned joint District Judge came to an incorrect decision in reversing the trial Court's judgment. There is brother in the facts or evidence to show or justify the issue taken by the lower appellate Court with the Court with the petitioners possession or the lack of it of the suit land at all material times and their dispossession there from and in that regard, the learned joint District Judge is found to have erred in law in reaching an erroneous decision to reverse the trial Court's judgment. The learned joint District Judge failed to no to that the petitioners having been better able to prove their title and possession in the suit land as compared to the opposite party No.1 and that the trial Court properly and sufficiently adjudged the matter in favour of the petitioners.
